title: einvoice conformance rules (v1)
description: Machine-readable JSON Schema for the rules export emitted at einvoice/export/rules.json by einvoice/gen_export.py. This is the adopter-facing catalog of every EN 16931 / XRechnung business rule the engine asserts, each with its family, blocking severity, the syntax it fires in, the plain-language remediation title/fix, and the per-syntax (UBL/CII) Schematron provenance that differentially proved it. Every field is copied verbatim from the committed machine sources (coverage_matrix.json + remediation_catalog.json); the export invents no rule claim. The top-level `schemaVersion` integer is pinned to 1 for this v1 schema (mirrors the report's report_version const); a breaking change to the export shape bumps both `schemaVersion` and this $id to v2. Subschemas are inlined (no $ref) so the stdlib structural validator exercises every constraint.

generated_by.description: The generator that emitted this file (einvoice/gen_export.py).

provenance.description: Where the rows came from - a do-not-hand-edit note and the committed source JSONs the export was derived from.

note.description: Human note stating the file is generated and not to be hand-edited.

sources.description: The committed machine-source filenames this export was projected from.

rule_count.description: Number of rule entries in `rules` (kept consistent with len(rules)).

schemaVersion.description: Export shape version; pinned to 1 for this v1 schema.

rules.description: One entry per asserted business rule.

family.description: The rule family, e.g. 'core', 'xrechnung-cius', 'xrechnung-extension', 'peppol-kosit-vendored', 'xrechnung-cvd-tmp'. Free string (families may be added); consumers should not assume a closed set.

syntax.description: Which syntax(es) the rule fires in.

severity.description: Blocking severity derived from the official @flag.

title.description: Plain-language rule title from the remediation catalog.

remediation.description: The plain-language remediation for the rule.

bindings.description: Per-syntax Schematron provenance. At least one of `ubl`/`cii` is present (a rule fires in the syntax(es) named by `syntax`).

ubl.description: UBL Schematron provenance for this rule.

differentially_proven.description: True iff this rule was differentially proven to fire against the official artifact.

sch.description: Path to the Schematron artifact the rule was proven against.

suite.description: The standards suite, e.g. 'CEN EN 16931' / 'KoSIT XRechnung'.

asserts.description: OPTIONAL: the concrete Schematron assert ids this rule maps to when the artifact splits it across several asserts.

note.description: OPTIONAL: a human note explaining a non-1:1 mapping between the rule and the artifact.

cii.description: CII Schematron provenance for this rule.
